scope: The B8c lane's checks of the TOPPBase remainder (2026-09-27): ParamXMLFile::store's text of floating-point items, list items and restrictions and of 64-bit integers (tests/data/b8c_release/ini: numbers.ini, specials.ini); ParamEntry::isValid and Param::update on 64-bit integer values, and GaussTraceFitter::setParameters with max_iteration beyond int (width.tsv, trace.tsv); ParamJSONFile::load on 115 JSON documents that take every path of nlohmann::json 3.11.2's scanner and parser a load can meet, with the exception class and what() of each refusal and the values of each success (tests/data/b8c_release/json).
method: ParamXMLFile.cpp, Param.cpp, ParamValue.cpp, StringUtils.cpp, NumericFormatting.h, ParamJSONFile.cpp and the vendored nlohmann_json lexer.hpp and parser.hpp read at the core pin with git show. A driver (driver.cpp) built on the node with the Release install's compiler and libOpenMS's own core flags (the recipe of ../oracle/sne-completion/remote_run.sh) runs four modes, each in a clean environment (env -i, a per-run HOME and OPENMS_HOME_PATH, OPENMS_DISABLE_UPDATE_CHECK=ON, OPENMS_DATA_PATH pinned): numbers stores two parameter trees with ParamXMLFile; width prints isValid's verdict and message and update's success, stored value and log for eight and four cases; trace sets six max_iteration values on a GaussTraceFitter; json loads each document of json_cases.tsv (written by make_inputs.py) onto a tree with T:1:d, T:1:i, T:1:s, T:1:a:d and T:1:dl and writes the exception's class and what() byte for byte. Everything ran twice (run1, run2); results/differ.txt is empty, every file of the two runs is identical. run1 is retained under tests/data/b8c_release and replayed by tests/topp_write_ini_text.rs (source_number_text_is_the_release_builds), tests/param_int_width.rs and tests/param_json_syntax.rs.
evidence_tier: oracle-generated (tier 1 executed differential) against the Release build. One documented difference: a byte of nlohmann::json's 'last read' that is not UTF-8 is U+FFFD in this port's message, which is text (the tests compare against the Release bytes read lossily).
